checkpoint_review: I have re-evaluated the 'Enormous bill with distensible gular pouch' checkpoint. While the Router marked this as present, my independent visual inspection confirms the bill structure is anatomically correct for a Brown Pelican in flight (where the pouch is often retracted/flat against the neck). The shape is distinct and elongated. I maintain the 'Checked' verdict but acknowledge the lack of 'distension' is behavioral, not an artifact. The 'Wings contrasting lighter body' failure is definitively due to species mismatch (Brown Pelican has dark body), not generation error. All other Router verdicts hold up under scrutiny.
authenticity_review: The Pose Auditor's HIGH risk flag (47% low confidence) was initially concerning, but upon visual verification, many low-confidence keypoints correspond to the bird's tucked legs and obscured face features which are naturally difficult to detect in this pose/species. However, the wing tip fusion (Router severity 2) is visually confirmed—the primary feathers merge into a single mass rather than showing individual separation. The water interface blur (severity 1) is also present but could be motion blur; I will treat it as a minor artifact. The 'waxy' texture on the head is less severe than initially thought; it resembles photographic compression/sharpening artifacts common in wildlife photography. I am adjusting the authenticity score upward slightly to reflect that the major structural elements are sound and the artifacts are localized to edges/textures.
